A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPAD research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content and distinguishing the added checklist from scientific additions.

before.justification: v2 reports original IPAD detection experiments, component ablations, a ten-participant interpretability study, and an appendix analyzing linguistic differences between inferred prompts.

after.justification: v3 retains original detection results, ablations, and the ten-participant study. These establish original empirical results despite the checklist's contradictory statement that no human subjects were involved.

M1.justification: The Prompt Inverter, PTCV, RC, Phi-3 backbone, LoRA training, regeneration procedure, and probability fusion remain unchanged, including weight 0.45 and threshold 0.54. Algorithm 1 moves from the appendix into the methodology without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Training datasets, detection domains, structured-prompt benchmarks, attack scenarios, and the appendix's XSum/WritingPrompts/PubMedQA evaluations are retained. The removed linguistic analysis reused existing in-distribution and OOD samples rather than introducing distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged across the detection, prompt-inversion, distinguisher, and DPIC comparisons. Scribbr, QuillBot, and GPTZero are now named explicitly but were already identified through v2's links. Newly discussed detectors in related work are not added to the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Removing Appendix G also removes its evaluation design: 1,000 prompts per text origin, 220 LFTK features, and LIWC-based variables assessed partly through ChatGPT. Retained benchmark protocols and the ten-participant study are unchanged. Temperature zero is newly disclosed, without evidence of a changed prior setting.

E4.justification: v3 removes the supplementary investigation of syntactic complexity, pronoun usage, and analytical thinking in inferred HWT versus LGT prompts from v2 Appendix G. Component ablations, robustness tests, the user study, and IPAD/DPIC examples remain; Figure 3 is identical.

E5.justification: The deleted linguistic analysis removes its reporting of three features with p-values below 0.05. v3's checklist newly explains the absence of error bars by asserting deterministic results at temperature zero, but supplies no new uncertainty estimates, repeated-run counts, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–6 and 8–9, Figures 2–3, and the user-study ratings remain unchanged. Appendix G's linguistic findings disappear, including the reported 75 versus 2 second-person-pronoun occurrences per 1,000 HWT-derived versus LGT-derived prompts.

T1.justification: The probability normalization, fusion equations, AUROC formula, and computational-complexity argument are retained. The complexity discussion receives its own subsection, while the AUROC appendix is renumbered. No substantive mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain inverse-prompt detection with two distinguishers, robustness across the same settings, and improved interpretability and trust. Headline performance claims are unchanged. The revised title and concluding paradigm language do not extend claims already present in v2.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly interprets RC as local alignment with greater attack sensitivity and PTCV as global distribution matching with greater robustness. Interpretations concerning linguistic differences between HWT- and LGT-derived prompts disappear with Appendix G. The existing limitations concerning in-context examples and computational cost remain.

D1.justification: The new checklist discloses temperature zero and mentions one A800-80GB GPU plus a V100, while the main text retains training on six A800 GPUs. v3 also revises the stated code address and removes LFTK/LIWC processing details with Appendix G. These are documentation changes, not evidence that retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 adds discussion and citations for Lastde, Glimpse, and MAGRET and explicitly distinguishes regeneration-based detection. Additional introductory and dataset citations appear. The central positioning against DPIC and existing prompt-extraction approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact. Local changes include the title and author information, rewritten detector-related work, an expanded conclusion, a separate complexity subsection, relocation of Algorithm 1, integration of limitations into the conclusion, and an appended conference checklist.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column format with a predominantly single-column conference layout, substantially reflows tables and captions, and relocates Algorithm 1 into the methodology. Figure 2 is redrawn with different colors, typography, and axis ticks. These are extensive visual changes despite retained plotted results.

improvement.justification: Clearer algorithm placement, updated related work, and additional settings disclosures provide modest benefits. However, removing the linguistic analysis reduces supporting evidence for the prompt-interpretability discussion, and checklist items 14–15 deny human-subject research despite the retained ten-participant study in Section 3.3. These losses in explanatory support and reporting consistency produce a limited overall decline; the core method and benchmark evidence remain intact.
